summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of atrial fibrillation, multiple CVAs, tracheostomy, ileostomy, diabetes, and recurrent infections was admitted after a respiratory arrest due to mucus plugging. He was transferred from an outside facility where he required CPR and suctioning of a large mucus plug. CT imaging revealed multifocal lung opacities concerning for aspiration or pneumonia. He was treated with IV antibiotics for Pseudomonas and Proteus from sputum cultures and fluconazole for a yeast urinary tract infection. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic administration. His mental status improved, and he was weaned to lower oxygen support. Repeat imaging showed resolving lung opacities. He was discharged to extended care on oral antibiotics, with instructions to continue Coumadin and monitor INR, manage pain, and care for his tracheostomy and skin.
problems: Pneumonitis due to inhalation of food or vomitus
